summary: The revision keeps the main arc and most protected epigrams, and it keeps the chapter's key dependencies. Several compressions leave residue or distort: Dante is still invoked without his tercet, Gibbon's 'one felt also the relation' is cut, the planned Amiens/Ruskin material is thinned, and the 1895 and force statements lose some qualification. The revision also cuts more than the plan's optional items and drops several 'essential' items (Lucretius gloss, the Berlin/Marx payoff, the Cellini half-natures setup).

coverage.assessment: The Bacon sentence is trimmed and the Lucretius/Dante comparison is left unsupported by any Dante text. Gibbon's 'relation' remark was dropped. Langley's 'not responsible' attitude survives.
Langley is identified, and the Amiens trip and St. Gaudens are clear. 'He' in P14 is St. Gaudens and reads acceptably.
There is no dialogue in the chapter; the quoted Gibbon and Lucretius lines are intact.

Langley's modest admission about the sun's uncertain heat is cut. The 'Adams knew nothing about any of it' sentence merges Virgin and radium into a vague 'it'. The Lucretius line is left with no gloss.
The retrospective narrator and hedges ('perhaps himself', 'risk translating') are preserved.
The dynamo paragraph loses its closing epigram ('not so human as some, but the most expressive'). The 'knife-edge/Lancelot' passage and several semicolon series are flattened.

The Adams/St. Gaudens contrast is weakened: the Cellini 'child of' pair stays, but the 'half of a nature' setup is thinner, and the Ruskin and Gibbon lesson loses its point. The 'channel of force/taste' antithesis survives.
All five dependencies survive locally; see below.

findings.title: Dante invoked but not quoted; Lucretius left unglossed
findings.claim: The Dante tercet was cut, as the plan permits, yet 'invoked Venus exactly as Dante invoked the Virgin' remains with no Dante text. The Latin line has no gloss, though the plan asks for a clear gloss.
findings.reader_effect: The comparison is asserted rather than shown, and a reader without Latin cannot follow it.

evidence.quote: where the poet invoked Venus exactly as Dante invoked the Virgin:--
Donna, sei tanto grande, e tanto vali

findings.counterevidence: The plan allows the cut if the comparison is kept, and the comparison is kept.
findings.plan_relation: The plan's gloss requirement was missed.
findings.minimal_repair: Add a short gloss after the Latin, e.g. 'who alone governs the nature of things'; optionally restore one Dante line.

findings.title: Gibbon/Ruskin lesson thinned
findings.claim: 'but besides the humor, one felt also the relation' and the Ruskin comparison ('more instructive than a whole lecture of Ruskin') were cut. 'One sees what one brings' now follows only 'Gibbon ignored the Virgin', so Gibbon's humor and its meaning are not tied together.
findings.reader_effect: The echo of the earlier mirror passage survives, but its payoff is weaker.

evidence.quote: One sees what one brings, and at that moment Gibbon brought the French Revolution.
but besides the humor, one felt also the relation.

findings.counterevidence: The essential phrase, the Gibbon quotation, and the humor of the fat historian all remain.
findings.plan_relation: Optional trimming, but it hits a protected dependency.
findings.minimal_repair: Restore 'but besides the humor, one felt also the relation.'

findings.title: Final 'it' blurs Virgin and radium; Langley's uncertainty lost
findings.claim: 'Adams knew nothing about any of it' lost the source's 'any of them' (Virgin, radium and the other forces). Langley's admission that the sun might 'spout less or more' was cut.
findings.reader_effect: The chapter's closing claim about the Virgin being 'easiest to handle' loses its comparative frame with radiant matter, and Langley's modesty is thinner.

evidence.quote: Adams knew nothing about any of it, but though all were occult
It could scarcely be more complex than radium

findings.counterevidence: 'all were occult' still points to plural forces.
findings.plan_relation: Planned compression; the ambiguity is a side effect.
findings.minimal_repair: Write 'about any of them' and add 'as complex as radium'.

findings.title: Dynamo-hall and rupture passages flattened
findings.claim: The dynamo paragraph now ends on the prayer and loses 'the most expressive'. The revision also loses 'the force was wholly new', the sun's heat passage, and the knife-edge/Lancelot image.
findings.reader_effect: The central paragraphs end less on Adams's epigrammatic cadence, and the hazard of the new education is less vivid.

evidence.quote: inherited instinct taught the natural expression of man before silent and infinite force.

findings.counterevidence: The prayer image and baby image survive, and the plan marks them as essential.
findings.minimal_repair: Restore the closing sentence, 'Among the thousand symbols... the most expressive.'

findings.title: Marx and Berlin payoff, 'sex' qualifiers
findings.claim: Marx is kept but the 'moral issue set aside' ending ('He cared nothing for the sex of the dynamo') is cut. The 'any one brought up among Puritans' premise now follows directly after the fig-leaf remark.
findings.reader_effect: Minor loss of Adams's humorous detachment and of the dynamo-sex link.

evidence.quote: did not concern one who was studying the relations of unmoral force.
He cared nothing for the sex of the dynamo until he could measure its energy.

findings.counterevidence: 'unmoral force' is kept, as the plan requires.
findings.minimal_repair: Restore the final sentence if space allows.

dependencies.assessment: The backward link to Chicago 1893 is kept.

evidence.quote: since 1893, when he began the study at Chicago.

dependencies.assessment: Langley is identified as 'of the Smithsonian' and is the teacher.

evidence.quote: Langley, of the Smithsonian, came by, and showed it to him.

dependencies.assessment: The 310/Constantine comparison is kept in its single sentence.

evidence.quote: that of 310, when Constantine set up the Cross.

dependencies.assessment: The 'what one brings' line and the St. Gaudens force/taste contrast are preserved. The partner's 'mirror' line is in the existing neighbor draft.
Chartres is kept as the site of the Virgin's force and as the turn to scholastic study. The partner also mentions Chartres.

strengths: Protected epigrams survive intact: 'American Virgin would never dare command', 'channel of force/taste', and 'All the steam in the world... Chartres'.
The sequence list (men, society, time, thought, force) is in order before the broken neck.
The closing pen/blind-man's-dog passage and the January 19, 1901 Cherbourg sailing are preserved.
